resolution_rule: Resolve the predecessor state chain first, then add new_assessments below. Apply scope_updates and candidate_reconciliations without double-counting semantically identical source updates. No prior clean assessment is deleted or silently overwritten.

o_snapshot.delta: O main is unchanged from the predecessor comparator snapshot. No configured or pending O work is promoted to evaluated evidence. Prior O-side judgments remain stable unless the clean candidate changed.

status_definitions.known: O explicitly encodes/discusses materially the same idea but no direct behavioral measurement of this clean mechanism/scope was found.
status_definitions.evaluated: O has direct explicit experiment/evidence on substantially the same mechanism under a named matched scope.
status_definitions.partially_tested: O measured or implemented a related adaptation/submechanism, but not the full clean mechanism or transfer scope.
status_definitions.uncovered: No materially equivalent O mechanism/direct test was found; generic adjacency is insufficient.

continual_learning.mechanism: Use a label-independent HSIC distribution-shift signal to create new continual-learning experts without task IDs or ground-truth boundary labels.
continual_learning.scope: Ye & Bors, Neurocomputing 2025. EEM-SD Split MNIST/CIFAR10/CIFAR100 accuracy 97.02±0.17/59.03±0.23/23.26±0.14. Expert counts 21/25/7 for benchmarks with 5/5/20 class-incremental tasks; threshold tuning strongly changes expansion and capacity can reach about 5.3e8 parameters on CIFAR10.

provenance.source: Ye & Bors, Evolving Ensemble Model based on Hilbert Schmidt Independence Criterion for task-free continual learning, 2025

continual_learning.uncertainty: Image-classification streams; expansion is not a calibrated one-to-one task detector and architecture growth is large. Same-label agent/LLM domain shift is untested.
continual_learning.o_comparison: No HSIC-based task-free neural boundary detector, expert expansion controller or matched experiment exists in O.

continual_learning.mechanism: Combine lightweight class prototypes with per-parameter online hypergradient reweighting to turn offline prompt methods into task-free single-pass continual learners.
continual_learning.scope: Michel et al., TMLR 2026. CODA/CIFAR100 15.14±3.78 baseline to 44.21±8.04 with prototypes+FGH; prototypes alone 31.27±6.95 and FGH alone 22.27±5.88 in the cited setting, showing component synergy rather than a universal hypergradient gain.

provenance.source: From Offline to Online Memory-Free and Task-Free Continual Learning via Fine-Grained Hypergradients, TMLR 2026

continual_learning.uncertainty: Class-incremental vision with labels/prototypes; task-free means no boundary/task ID, not label-free. Hyperparameter dependence remains material.
continual_learning.o_comparison: O has no prototype-based continual parameter learner or fine-grained hypergradient update mechanism.

continual_learning.mechanism: Use a fixed-budget short-term FIFO plus long-term distribution-matching replay split to preserve a learned world model across changing observations, dynamics and rewards.
continual_learning.scope: ARROW, TMLR 2026, fixed total replay budget 2^19 observations. Atari default forgetting 0.115 versus DreamerV3 2.263 and WC-ACC 0.470 versus -0.141; CoinRun default forgetting 0.154 versus 0.416 and WC-ACC 0.539 versus 0.263. Buffer-ratio ablation exposes a stability/plasticity tradeoff.

provenance.source: ARROW: Augmented Replay for RObust World models, TMLR 2026

continual_learning.uncertainty: World-model RL evidence, not an LLM-agent memory experiment; no replay split dominates every setting.
continual_learning.o_comparison: O persists execution/evidence state but has no learned world-model replay buffer or matched continual-RL experiment.

cross_field.mechanism: Choose constrained diagnostic excitation for model components that matter to downstream control quality instead of maximizing generic information everywhere.
cross_field.scope: Larsson et al., Journal of Process Control 2015 industrial depropanizer. Deliberate model degradation moves p(theta) 0.0082 to 0.043; MPC-X re-identification restores acceptable simulated and improved real-plant performance, but the real plant lacks a clean randomized passive-learning matched baseline.

provenance.source: Experimental evaluation of model predictive control with excitation on an industrial depropanizer, 2015

cross_field.uncertainty: Strong physical feasibility/restoration evidence, not a clean passive-baseline effect size; transfer to research-agent experimentation is hypothetical.
cross_field.o_comparison: O values decision-changing information but has no application-oriented active-identification/excitation controller or matched experiment.

cross_field.mechanism: Checkpoint only at observable state-changing semantic boundaries, choose checkpoint granularity from changed state, and overlap persistence with naturally idle latency.
cross_field.scope: Crab 2026 preprint. More than 75% of turns have no recovery-relevant state; skip ratio up to 87%; chat-only recovery correctness 8% versus 100% with semantic checkpointing; checkpoint traffic down up to 87%; crashed execution within 1.9% of fault-free; every-turn full checkpointing up to 3.78x at high density.

provenance.source: Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes, 2026

cross_field.uncertainty: Agent-sandbox preprint; benefit depends on correct recovery-relevant side-effect classification.
cross_field.o_comparison: O already uses semantic/runtime durability boundaries, deterministic journals and restart-safe recovery, but has no OS-side-effect classifier, tiered checkpoint-granularity controller or Crab-style matched traffic/recovery benchmark.

cross_field.mechanism: Randomly sample a small unbiased subset of diagnostic predicates per run and aggregate statistically across many runs instead of tracing everything every time.
cross_field.scope: Cooperative Bug Isolation / Statistical Debugging. In the bc case, instrumentation overhead falls from about 13% to about 0.5% at 1/1000 predicate sampling; deployment material also reports roughly 10,000-20,000 runs may be needed for accurate diagnosis at 1/100 sampling.
cross_field.uncertainty: Trades per-run observability for population sample complexity; poor fit for rare failures without adaptive density. Agent transfer untested.
cross_field.o_comparison: O records detailed execution events but has no randomized inclusion-probability telemetry or population statistical fault-localization mechanism.

evaluation.mechanism: Use pre-specified group-sequential testing with valid alpha spending and explicit practical margins/precision targets to stop evaluation when evidence is sufficient or futile.
evaluation.scope: Stop Guessing When to Stop Testing, 2026. Across 206 VLMs/31 benchmarks, about 15%/30%/50% of samples suffice for ±3/±2/±1.5 point confidence widths; fixed 1.2K samples resolve 55% of 1,000 top-model pairs versus 76% sequentially; >2-point gaps typically save at least 60% evaluation effort.
evaluation.uncertainty: Independence/normality and multiple-comparison assumptions need clustered long-horizon extensions; margins are user-chosen.
evaluation.o_comparison: O has evidence gates and budgets but no group-sequential alpha-spending/MDE stopping mechanism or matched evaluation-efficiency study.

evaluation.mechanism: Localize the earliest unrecoverable failure with explicit constraints and step-indexed violation logs, and choose whole-trajectory versus localized judging by horizon.
evaluation.scope: AgentRx 2026, 115 failed trajectories. On tau-bench, step accuracy 32.2±3.2 to 54.0±1.6, category 25.3±1.6 to 40.2±1.6 and mean step distance 5.7 to 2.4; 68% of Magentic-One trajectories contain at least two failures. Long-context gains are weaker and one-shot versus stepwise protocol depends on horizon.
evaluation.uncertainty: Generated constraints can be wrong; no calibrated abstention guarantee and transfer beyond three domains is untested.
evaluation.o_comparison: O persists full action/tool traces and uses scoped task evaluation/fresh repair cycles, a related process-attribution substrate, but has no earliest-unrecoverable-failure metric, violation-log judge or horizon-conditioned judging experiment.

evaluation.mechanism: Let a process verifier query/re-execute the environment and distinguish correct, recoverable and irrecoverable intermediate states; test it under actual selection/search pressure.
evaluation.scope: DataPRM 2026. Ternary rewards {0,0.5,1}; 100-example human check 86.0% agreement/kappa .83. Qwen3-235B Best-of-N DataPRM-4B averages 37.11/39.77/40.89 at N=4/8/16 while a general math PRM is 30.22/31.33/29.11; beam scaling can degrade the generic PRM while DataPRM improves.
evaluation.uncertainty: Agentic data-analysis domain with task-specific PRM; portability and evaluator dependence remain unresolved.
evaluation.o_comparison: O uses deterministic/external checks and actual action traces, so environment-grounded verification is partially represented, but O has no learned ternary PRM or search-pressure verifier study.

evaluation.mechanism: Calibrate process-reward scores against Monte Carlo completions from the actual downstream policy and use conservative calibrated probabilities for abstention/backtracking or compute allocation.
evaluation.scope: NeurIPS 2025 PRM calibration. MATH500 Llama-3.2-1B Brier .2414 to .0692 and AdaptiveCE .2830 to .0811; OOD AIME Brier .194 to .003. Calibrated instance-adaptive sampling recovers near fixed Best-of-64 accuracy with materially lower budget on several MATH500 policies.

provenance.source: Know What You Don’t Know, arXiv:2506.09338

evaluation.uncertainty: Math PRMs; agent/tool transfer untested and calibration is policy-conditional.
evaluation.o_comparison: O has qualitative UNCERTAIN/fail-close semantics but no PRM probability model, Monte Carlo policy-conditioned calibration or calibrated compute allocator.

evaluation.mechanism: Use heterogeneous reward-model unanimity with abstention on disagreement when false labels are more costly than reduced coverage, and report reliability jointly with coverage.
evaluation.scope: CUARewardBench 2025/2026: 272 trajectory and 346 step expert annotations. Unanimous ensemble outcome precision/NPV 89.8/93.3; process precision/NPV/recall/specificity 81.7/85.1/48.9/24.4, exposing a large coverage tradeoff.
evaluation.uncertainty: Computer-use VLM judges and short trajectories; unanimity is not universally preferable and requires an explicit utility/cost model.
evaluation.o_comparison: O can return UNCERTAIN but has no heterogeneous judge ensemble, unanimity rule or measured precision/coverage tradeoff.

failure_evidence.mechanism: Audit benchmark task validity/composition because filtering flagged tasks can reverse model rankings even when the exact stored trajectories are unchanged.
failure_evidence.scope: AgentSuite ICML 2026 public artifacts. Tau-bench top two reverse after Filtering; ACEBench Kimi-K2 versus Gemini-2.5-Pro reverses; overall Kimi rank 2 to 3 and o3-high 3 to 2. Filtering rescored the same Original trajectories and changed only the surviving audited task set.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Filtering policy is not proof every dropped task is invalid; Fixed reruns answer a different question and partial-coverage rows require care.
failure_evidence.o_comparison: O already treats benchmark/scorer validity and contamination as first-class and uses protected/hidden evidence, a related submechanism, but has no AgentSuite-style audited-task rank-stability measurement.

failure_evidence.mechanism: Treat live-web benchmark validity and scores as environment/version dependent; pin task version, browser/system/region and other execution provenance before longitudinal comparison.
failure_evidence.scope: Online-Mind2Web replaced 36/300 tasks on 2025-11-03 due invalidity/CAPTCHA and later replaced additional tasks. Mind2Web-Live with the same named gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 planner reports success 16.5% US/Windows/Chrome, 20.2% US/Windows/Firefox, 8.65% UK/Windows/Chrome and 21.2% Singapore/Windows/Chrome; no randomized repeated confidence analysis is supplied.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Task replacement combines multiple causes; configuration table demonstrates sensitivity, not isolated causal effects. Same-policy calendar-repeat evidence remains open.
failure_evidence.o_comparison: O tracks source versions/clocks, freshness, environment and execution provenance, a related submechanism, but has no live-web temporal/configuration sensitivity benchmark.

failure_evidence.mechanism: Audit self-correction for harness-role conditioning: a byte-identical wrong claim may be explicitly rejected when presented as external context but not when represented as the model's own prior thought.
failure_evidence.scope: The Self-Correction Illusion, 2026. Across 13 model-domain cells, moving a byte-identical wrong claim from self-thought to an external role raises explicit correction by 23-93 percentage points; e.g. Llama-3.3-70B generated logic 0% baseline to +93.3pp under neutral user-role relabeling. n=30 paired tasks/cell.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Measures explicit error flagging, not guaranteed final-answer improvement; assumes the error is localized and external-role trust can itself be unsafe.
failure_evidence.o_comparison: No message-role relabeling self-correction experiment or role-conditioned error-addressability mechanism was found in O.

long_horizon.mechanism: Evaluate failure-monitor interventions by baseline failure prevalence p, recovery rate r and disruption rate d, because high detector AUROC can coexist with negative end-to-end value; net success change is p*r-(1-p)*d.
long_horizon.scope: Accurate Failure Prediction in Agents Does Not Imply Effective Failure Prevention, 2026. Overall critic AUROC .936/F1 .963, yet best intervention deltas include HotPotQA -2.3/0/-25.5pp and GAIA -4.4/-4.4/-30.0pp across three agents; ALFWorld gives only +0.5 to +2.8pp. Oracle upside in tested systems is only about 4-8pp because recovery capacity is limiting.
long_horizon.uncertainty: Model/benchmark/intervention specific; high AUROC is not itself harmful and the p/r/d threshold must be re-estimated per deployment.
long_horizon.o_comparison: O already requires scoped/reversible candidate interventions, protected regression evidence and actual outcomes, so harmful-intervention control is partially represented, but it has no explicit p/r/d operating-curve measurement for learned failure monitors.

long_horizon.mechanism: Layer deterministic verifiable invariants with a calibrated learned telemetry monitor, then close detection into rollback+rerun repair and measure final task recovery.
long_horizon.scope: Real-Time Detection and Repair of LLM Agent Failures, 2026-08-03. Learned monitor AUROC .872; cold transfer .527 versus .885 after recalibration. Deterministic verification catches 60% of failures, 96% with coverage check, with 0/63 false positives in the cited evaluation. Rollback+rerun recovers 45% versus 16% resampling and raises task success 52% to 73% at roughly one extra model call/run.
long_horizon.uncertainty: Primary abstract-level quantitative evidence; learned monitor requires deployment recalibration and deterministic coverage depends on available invariants.
long_horizon.o_comparison: O has deterministic checks, checkpointed recovery and fail-closed validation, related submechanisms, but no learned telemetry monitor plus live rollback/rerun repair study.

long_horizon.mechanism: Classify effects as idempotent, reversible, compensable or irreversible before execution and roll back to the earliest conflicting compensable/irreversible action while accounting for compensation and wasted-work cost.
long_horizon.scope: Revisable by Design, 2026. StreamBench DeepSeek-V3 n=1,008; Revision Absorber quality is reported statistically indistinguishable from Full-Restart while wasting 14.6x fewer completed steps. Theory states conflicting irreversible actions can make full revised-goal satisfaction impossible.
long_horizon.uncertainty: Theory assumptions and StreamBench transfer need validation; compensability is domain/tool specific.
long_horizon.o_comparison: O already separates side effects from replay, uses idempotency/fencing and pre-dispatch authorization, but has no explicit I/R/K/X action taxonomy, compensation ledger or earliest-conflict rollback evaluation.

multi_agent.mechanism: Keep semi-independent evolutionary lineages and make exchange cadence, exchange size and acceptance policy controlled variables rather than always-on broadcast.
multi_agent.scope: EvoDiverse 2026 fixed-budget Physics sweep: period2/5 Best Acc@0.1=.5 versus period10/20=.3; at period5 k=5 and k=10 both .5 while k=1=.3. MH-gated exchange Physics best=.416 versus isolated ensemble .333 and random swap .346; exact optimum is algorithm/domain dependent.
multi_agent.uncertainty: Parallel-tempering LLM search; no universal cadence or topology optimum.
multi_agent.o_comparison: No multi-population island/exchange controller or selective migration experiment exists in O.

multi_agent.mechanism: Use cheap broad stochastic fitness only for triage and escalate plausible champions/uncertain comparisons to higher-fidelity evaluation before selection/archive replacement.
multi_agent.scope: FAMOU 2026. Three-game fast evaluation has Spearman rho=.11 (p=.69) versus 20-40-game deeper ranking. Single-run component ablation reports full combined score .521 and without deep evaluation .385 (-26.0%, p=.002), the largest individual drop; main comparisons are equal-iteration, not equal-compute.
multi_agent.uncertainty: Adversarial-game domain; component interactions and unequal compute limit causal generalization.
multi_agent.o_comparison: O has evidence tiers and candidate evaluation but no measured cheap-fitness/deep-fitness escalation scheduler or rank-correlation gate.

multi_agent.mechanism: Measure evaluator error correlation/effective independent vote count before spending budget on judge panels; nominal judge count is not evidence count.
multi_agent.scope: Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes, 2026. Nine judges on 1,000 ChaosNLI-MNLI items have Kish n_eff=2.18 [2.07,2.31], mean error correlation .391±.111 and majority 72.0% versus best single 71.8%. RewardBench n_eff=1.99 and best single 95.5% exceeds panel 92.7%; chain-of-thought does not decorrelate errors in the study.
multi_agent.uncertainty: Classification/preference evaluation, not direct open-ended evolutionary search; heuristic n_eff thresholds are not universal collapse thresholds.
multi_agent.o_comparison: No LLM judge panel, error-correlation estimator or effective-vote budgeting mechanism was found in O.

neuroscience.mechanism: Use local spike-timing distributions and modified anti-Hebbian STDP to align feedback weights toward reciprocal forward weights without exact weight transport.
neuroscience.scope: Nature Communications 2026 SAL. Deep SymmNet, five seeds/200 epochs: CIFAR10 BP83.8±0.3, SAL79.6±0.4, FA69.5±0.7; Fashion-MNIST BP92.1±0.1, SAL91.5±0.2; SVHN BP93.5±0.1, SAL91.5±0.1. Only fully connected feedback weights are SAL/RDD-symmetrized; non-BP conv layers use FA. Public code lacks inspected raw five-seed sweep results.
neuroscience.uncertainty: Below BP in reported labels, partial deep-network weight-transport solution, no independent exact replication.
neuroscience.o_comparison: No spiking/STDP feedback-alignment neural-learning mechanism or experiment exists in O.

neuroscience.mechanism: Grow modular spiking subnetworks and cross-task links, then prune using a score combining local Hebbian co-activation and global cross-task reuse/generalization.
neuroscience.scope: TD-MCL, National Science Review 2026. Split CIFAR100 10-step 87.06±0.22 versus DER++84.20±0.47; 20-step 89.26±0.31 versus DER++86.60±0.50; Tiny-ImageNet 69.1±0.59 versus RDER68.8±0.54. Removing local Hebbian or global reuse terms lowers average incremental accuracy by 11.25% and 11.77% respectively. Explicit task segmentation is assumed.
neuroscience.uncertainty: Neuro-inspired engineering, not a demonstrated biological mechanism; explicit task boundaries, no independent replication, analytical rather than measured energy numbers.
neuroscience.o_comparison: No spiking modular continual-learning growth/pruning mechanism or matched experiment exists in O.

open_source.mechanism: Separate production from durable-state admission: a reviewer/verifier checks artifacts against explicit criteria and task-native evidence before reusable state is committed; failed routes remain negative evidence and contradictions can trigger replan/rollback.
open_source.scope: Microsoft ArgusAgent 2026 public code/report. Full runtime reports about 78% on 731 SWE-Bench Pro tasks versus about 59% Direct Copilot at 1.41x aggregate tokens, but roles/routing/state/review/verification are bundled and no clean admission-gate-only causal ablation is available.
open_source.uncertainty: Architecture-level operational evidence; gate-specific effect size is unresolved and some enforcement may be prompt-mediated until code-path tracing is complete.
open_source.o_comparison: O directly implements scoped inactive Candidates, separate Candidate evaluation, protected regressions, objective evidence and rollbackable acceptance, so the admission-control submechanism is present; O has not reproduced Argus's reviewer/verifier workflow or its benchmark effect.

reasoning.mechanism: Adaptively choose among heterogeneous fresh proof generation, compiler-guided refinement, preserving the incumbent and stagnation-triggered resampling/restart under a budget.
reasoning.scope: Compiler-Guided Adaptive Proof Search, arXiv:2608.18084. Average pass rate +12.8pp and LLM calls -21.9% versus compared baseline setup; RLMEval-FLT3 39.3% at 13.5 calls/theorem versus Generalist pass@32 36.9%. Successful trajectories reject about 50.4% of proposed refinements; 39.5% of relevant solved trajectories verify from a preserved incumbent rather than newest proposal.
reasoning.uncertainty: Whole-proof Lean scope; pairwise progress judge is an LLM and total calls versus expensive generation cost differ. No tactic-level semantic diversity integration.
reasoning.o_comparison: O already fresh-replans failed units, preserves durable incumbent/evidence state and optimizes cost/risk, related control submechanisms, but has no Lean proof controller or matched compiler-guided exploration/refinement/restart experiment.

reasoning.mechanism: Audit proof-quality LLM judges for pairwise accuracy, swapped-order consistency and position bias instead of assuming proof-generation strength transfers to proof evaluation.
reasoning.scope: FormalRewardBench 2026, 250 Lean correct-vs-incorrect pairs. Best frontier LLM pairwise accuracy 59.8%; Claude Opus 4.5 correct-first 85.0% versus correct-second 69.7%, consistency 70.4%; DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B 94.9% versus 9.8%, consistency 9.9%.
reasoning.uncertainty: Finished correct-vs-incorrect proof ranking is not the same as judging repairability of two failed partial proofs.
reasoning.o_comparison: O treats evaluation as fallible and prefers objective evidence, but no formal-proof pairwise judge, swapped-order audit or position-bias measurement exists; generic evaluator caution is insufficient for this exact mechanism.

reasoning.mechanism: Expose schema-checked local dependency-graph proof edits as a cheaper repair action between raw patching and full rewrite, with theorem-prover validation after each edit.
reasoning.scope: BlueprintRepair 2026, BlueprintTrace 142 controlled failures. DeepSeek-V4-Flash typed edits solve 104/142, exact patches 109/142, full rewrites 104/142; patch cost/solved is 1.30x and rewrite 2.06x the typed interface. Typed edits nearly reach final coverage within 10k completion tokens/task.
reasoning.uncertainty: Controlled Lean blueprint failures; typed edits do not dominate patches in raw solved count and generic transfer is untested.
reasoning.o_comparison: O has scoped Candidates and repair loops but no theorem dependency-graph blueprint representation or typed local proof-edit interface.

reasoning.mechanism: Represent a proof plan as a dependency DAG, preserve already-proved nodes/signatures, and refine/decompose only failed nodes or wrong dependencies rather than regenerating solved structure.
reasoning.scope: Goedel-Architect 2026. DeepSeek-V4-Flash MiniF2F-test 99.2% pipeline pass@1; PutnamBench 75.6% after up to 16 internal refinement iterations. Initial blueprint solves 200/672 (29.8%); by iteration16, 508/672 (75.6%). Internal refinement compute means pipeline pass@1 is not one model sample.
reasoning.uncertainty: Formal theorem proving; control subsets/budgets differ and natural-language blueprint mode adds another pipeline.
reasoning.o_comparison: O preserves durable successful artifacts/continuations and repairs failed units without requiring global reset, related submechanisms, but has no theorem DAG, proved-node immutability contract or matched blueprint-refinement experiment.

self_improvement.mechanism: Treat multi-round skill evolution as sparse adaptive candidate search and audit validation-best replacements against released-test/transfer outcomes; ordinary best-validation selection is not a durable safety guarantee.
self_improvement.scope: Rethinking Self-Evolving Agent Skills, 2026. 42 feedback runs/14 settings: only 55/388 proposals become byte-distinct validation bests; validation selects evolved skills in 11/14 settings but only 9/11 improve released test. All 11 selected winners include failed trajectories. Public implementation repository excludes formal results/raw trajectories, so round-wise independent recomputation is currently blocked.
self_improvement.uncertainty: No direct greedy-vs-anytime-valid-vs-familywise gate comparison and no public 388-candidate trajectory deposit was found; released-test failures do not identify a single causal gate flaw.
self_improvement.o_comparison: O already uses scoped inactive Candidates, protected regressions, held-out/fresh boundaries and non-monotonic strategy review, so the adaptive-selection risk is partially represented, but no multi-round skill-evolution reliability curve or validation-to-released-test study is recorded.

self_improvement.mechanism: When the evaluator itself evolves, downstream optimized score cannot validate that evaluator; retain a locked outer audit inaccessible to the optimizing loop and test evaluator validity directly.
self_improvement.scope: Double Ratchet 2026. Evolved code-generation metric improves locked-set hidden-ground-truth agreement by +0.21 over bare judge (paired p=.014). Removing anchor guards collapses to a vacuous always-pass detector even though downstream skill training can still look similar; a report-generation Goodhart episode is caught by an independent judge. Held-out audits are small (~40-48 items) and three seeds.
self_improvement.uncertainty: Does not prove indefinitely calibrated self-evolving metrics; outer-audit frequency and teacher-family dependence remain open.
self_improvement.o_comparison: O explicitly separates internal/self evaluation from independent claim-grade evidence and does not allow internal tests or self-evaluation to establish AGI; that locked-outer-evidence principle is known, but O has no co-evolving metric experiment matching Double Ratchet.

self_improvement.mechanism: Evaluate persistent self-improvement substrates longitudinally with paired non-evolving controls and ablate skill-only, memory-only and combined retention because more memory is not automatically additive.
self_improvement.scope: FinEvo-Bench 2026, 120 finance tasks/20 scenes/six domains, same Qwen3.7-Max backbone across four scaffolds and three shuffled streams. Evolving conditions improve +9.33 to +19.37 points and reduce compliance issues by .12-.44/task; within Claude Code, skill-only outperforms memory-only and combined on quality/compliance. Exact full-table cells/variance remain a worker frontier.
self_improvement.uncertainty: Finance workflows may favor procedural skill retention; exact absolute substrate cells and cost/variance controls are not yet fully primary-verified.
self_improvement.o_comparison: O already persists memory/procedure state across workspace tasks and uses Episodes/Candidates for retention/transfer evidence, but has no matched memory-only versus skill-only versus combined substrate experiment.

candidate_reconciliations.reason: FE-023 is the same HAL reasoning-effort non-monotonicity mechanism already represented as FE-017; the new clean artifact tightens scope by stating that 21/36 means no improvement and includes ties, so it must not be restated as 21 strict regressions.

The disjoint 45/10/34 harness split and matched parallel/sequential controls are already part of C7's clean scope; current C9 re-expresses that same persistent-state held-out/fallback mechanism rather than adding a new semantic instance.

C11's artifact-quality -> activation/retrieval -> adherence -> outcome decomposition is materially the same staged uptake mechanism already represented in C1; the new study adds measured harness-load evidence rather than a new semantic mechanism.

scope_updates.update: HAL reasoning-effort evidence is now explicitly bounded as 21/36 matched cells with no accuracy improvement; ties are included, so do not call all 21 strict regressions. The result remains non-monotonic, not evidence that more reasoning generally harms agents.

Primary abstract still supports the qualitative aligned context+controlled-environment rewind mechanism, while exact 62.2/78.0/87.8 and component-ablation values remain secondary/indexed until primary table/source inspection. External/network/process side effects remain outside the rewind boundary.

Public code now sharpens ReasoningBank versus Memento: neither has an absolute retrieval threshold when memory is available. ReasoningBank SWE uses online sequential top-1 prior-task retrieval with <=3 generalized lessons injected in system context and an LLM induction-time success/failure judge; Memento defaults to top-8 concrete case+plan examples in a user message. Do not attribute EvoAgentBench's negative cell to one retrieval gate that does not exist in either public path.

MLReplicate resource/human-review evidence strengthens the boundary against raw compute as a quality proxy but remains cross-system observational. Only 10/37 valid automated-review submissions were accepted; 59% of automated accepts had fabricated/unsupported claims under human review; overall automated-vs-human rating Pearson r=.29/Spearman rho=.40, while soundness/contribution dimensions correlate more strongly (.77/.84).

EviGraph comparisons use the same qwen-3.6-plus backbone, sandbox and per-experiment time budget, but the paper explicitly says tightly coupled components make ordinary component ablation difficult. Package-level Overall 86.45%, CSR37.85% and EDC87.73% do not causally isolate typed graph, weak-node repair, rollback or memory; total compute/seeds remain incompletely specified.

ACRA directly ablates its critique agent on only eight procedures but exact figure values were not recovered. Procedure readiness classification is 67.5% on 39 manually checked procedures; among 150 ChemRnD procedures 99.33% reach syntactically valid XDL but only 94.67% pass source-discrepancy+hardware-simulation validation, reinforcing syntax != semantic/physical validity.

Rethinking Harness Evolution supplies explicit matched test-time and disjoint-transfer controls: without unit tests direct68.2/parallel72.3/sequential69.3/Harness Evolution67.4 average pass@1; with unit tests direct72.9/parallel86.0/sequential84.3/Harness Evolution75.8; disjoint test initial67.7 versus evolved68.3 (+0.6). Scope is Terminal-Bench-style and does not reject harness evolution globally.

Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit adds activation evidence to the existing experience->artifact->routing->uptake decomposition: evolver-side spread is <=3.1pp across tested benchmarks while weak Qwen3-32B loads relevant harness artifacts only about25% versus roughly96% for stronger models. This supports measuring activation/adherence separately from artifact quality.

comparison_guards: Each status is exact-mechanism/scope specific; narrow failures never reject a candidate family or untested configuration.
Configured/pending O work is not executed evidence.
Generic adjacent infrastructure does not count as evaluated evidence; partial status requires an implemented or measured related submechanism.
Current worker candidate IDs that restate an already represented semantic mechanism are reconciled as scope updates rather than double-counted.
No O, worker, PR, branch, CI or issue state was modified by this comparison.

coverage.exact_next_candidate: First new or semantically changed candidate artifact under research_workers_clean_g1/ after the recorded directory SHAs; if no worker delta exists, revalidate the first existing candidate materially affected by any O commit after e76c4e9d6d75c30769fc7c93ba6c1f0531779b46.
